title: Rachel was loved…
paragraphs:
Rachel was loved…
Leah was chosen to carry fruit.
And right there—Genesis breaks human logic.

Because we think love should equal blessing.
God often works the opposite way.

Rachel had what everyone wanted:
Beauty. Attention. Desire.
Scripture says Jacob loved her deeply (Genesis 29:18).
But her womb was closed.
Silence. Waiting. Emptiness.

Leah had what no one wants:
Rejection. Comparison. Being second.
“The Lord saw that Leah was unloved…” (Genesis 29:31)
So what did God do?
He opened her womb.

This isn’t random.
This is revelation.
God was exposing two different battles:

• Rachel’s battle → Idolatry of love
• Leah’s battle → Wound of rejection
And He dealt with both… differently.

Rachel said:
“Give me children, or I die!” (Genesis 30:1)

That’s not just desire—that’s desperation.
Her identity was collapsing.

She was loved by a man…
but still empty without what she wanted from God.
Leah?
At first, she named her sons out of pain:

“Now my husband will love me…”
“Surely he will be attached to me…”
But something shifts.

When Judah is born, she says:
“Now I will praise the Lord.” (Genesis 29:35)
No mention of Jacob.
No striving.
Just surrender.
That’s the turning point.

Leah stopped chasing human approval…
and started anchoring in God’s presence.
And from her line came:

• King David
• And ultimately… Jesus Christ
The Messiah did not come through the loved woman.
He came through the overlooked one.
Why?

Because God doesn’t build His story on human preference.
He builds it on surrendered hearts.
Here’s the truth:

You can be deeply loved by people…
and still be spiritually barren.

You can be overlooked, ignored, rejected…
and still be chosen by God to carry something eternal.

The deeper question isn’t:
“Who is loved more?”
It’s:
“Who is surrendered?”
And this is where the Gospel breaks in.
Because every one of us is Rachel and Leah.

• We crave validation
• We feel rejection
• We chase what we think will complete us
But none of it fills the void.
Only Jesus does.
Because the real barrenness is not physical—it’s spiritual.

We were all empty because of sin.
Cut off. Searching. Striving.
But through Jesus Christ:

• Sin is forgiven
• Identity is restored
• Purpose is reborn

Not because we were chosen by people…
but because we were redeemed by God.
And now?

Fruit doesn’t come from striving.
It comes from surrender.

Reflection:
Where are you still trying to earn what only God can give?

Shame doesn’t get the final word.
We Write Stories that Shame Tried to Erase.
